findings.issue_text: [High/performance] pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:~605 — Building the SQLite literal-ID IN list with repeated fmt.Sprintf copies an ever-growing SQL string, making 32,767-ID batch construction quadratic and causing massive transient allocations.

[Medium/performance] pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:~532 — Successful cleanup batches are logged at error level with the complete ids slice, producing enormous error log entries for 32,767-ID batches and adding formatting/I/O overhead while polluting error monitoring.

goldens.comment: The code uses Error log level for what appears to be debugging information. This will pollute error logs in production. Consider using Debug or Info level instead.

The cleanup job ticker was changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute, which can lead to increased database load and contention due to more frequent execution of cleanup tasks. This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with performance expectations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/performance] pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:~605 — Building the SQLite literal-ID IN list with repeated fmt.Sprintf copies an ever-growing SQL string, making 32,767-ID batch construction quadratic and causing massive transient allocations.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the code at lines 597-601 builds a SQL string by repeatedly concatenating with fmt.Sprintf in a loop: `values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)`. This is O(n²) string building because each iteration copies the entire accumulated string. With batch sizes up to 32,767 (as shown in the test case), this creates significant transient allocations. While this is a real performance concern in the new code, it's not a correctness bug - the code will still function correctly, just inefficiently. A strings.Builder would be the appropriate fix.
